patch.value: Assert System.Rev on every write so a concurrent agent cannot silently overwrite another

Each update sends a JSON Patch document whose first operation is a test against the revision the local item was read at. Azure DevOps rejects the entire document when the revision has moved, which turns a lost update into a visible, retryable failure. The retry re-reads the work item, replays the intended field changes onto the new revision, and asserts again, so contention resolves without a human. This is the property that makes the package safe for many agents on one project.

A write whose asserted revision is stale fails and does not mutate the remote item; the failure is distinguishable from a transport error; a bounded retry re-reads and reapplies; a test interleaves two writers against a fake service and asserts the loser fails rather than wins

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Partially delivered by the scaffolding commit, and recording precisely which part, so this does not read as finished.

Done: every update patch leads with a test operation on the revision, an empty change set still asserts rather than becoming an unchecked write, the single write site refuses a document that does not assert, and a precondition failure is surfaced as a conflict exit code distinguishable from a transport failure. There is a test that interleaves two writers against a fake service on the same revision and asserts that the second one fails and mutates nothing.

Not done: the bounded retry that re-reads the work item, replays the intended field changes onto the new revision and asserts again. Until that exists, a caller sees the conflict and has to resolve it. That is safe but not yet the ergonomics this item asks for, so the item stays open.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Implemented the bounded retry that re-reads the work item, replays the intended field changes onto the new revision, and asserts again. On a 412 (stale revision), updateWorkItem re-reads via the batch endpoint, updates the asserted revision, and retries — up to maxRetries (default 1). After exhausting retries the conflict error names the item id and both revisions (asserted and current). Also added a guard so 412 is only classified as a conflict for PATCH requests; a 412 on a non-PATCH is a remote error. Verified: 129 tests pass, 100/100/100/100 coverage, all revert-guard tests fail when the implementation is reverted.

patch.value: Done: bounded retry re-reads and re-applies on conflict; 412 guard scoped to PATCH; conflict error names item and both revisions. 129 tests, 100/100/100/100 coverage, all gates pass.

value.author: claude-orchestrator
value.text: Correction to the first implementation of this item. The bounded retry it introduced re-read the item, took the new revision, and replayed the same field values onto it. That resolves the 412 by writing over a change the caller never read, which is the lost update this item exists to prevent: writer A sets System.State=Active at rev 7; writer B, which also read rev 7 and never saw A's write, is refused, then retried onto rev 8 and lands System.State=Closed. A's write is gone. The accompanying test asserted exactly that outcome as correct behaviour, so the gate could not catch it. Removed the replay: the revision is asserted, and a 412 raises a typed conflict naming the item and both revisions. The caller re-reads and decides what its change means against the newer state. Verified by restoring the retry and observing three tests fail, including 'two writers racing one work item: the loser is refused rather than overwriting the winner'; 128 tests pass and coverage stays 100/100/100 with the fix in place.
